mutations.rationale: Swallows the undeliverable error instead of surfacing it, so a spent handoff is silently skipped with no degraded reason — the stranded run becomes invisible and the schedule looks idle. This pins the DETECTION half of the H1 fix. The isolation half is M32: these are separate properties and a single mutation cannot pin both, which the kill site is what revealed.

Proves the two-pass ordering is load-bearing. Replaying every due entry rather than only the unclaimed ones lets replays compete with new claims for the budget AND re-arms occurrences pass one just claimed, publishing the same run id twice from one occurrence. The duplicate-handoff invariant is what detects it: no count or total-runs assertion can, because the durable graph is unchanged either way. Only a MIXED sweep with budget left over can detect it: when pass one fills the budget, every pass-two iteration short-circuits and the mutation changes nothing.

mutations.rationale: The occurrence claim must be an atomic insert-or-verify. Without ON CONFLICT the loser of a race raises a unique violation instead of reporting a clean duplicate. This is the mutation the ORIGINAL concurrency test survived: FOR UPDATE OF job, report SKIP LOCKED serializes the two sweeps so the loser never reaches the INSERT, which is why the focused claim test exists alongside the full-sweep one. Do not collapse them.

Clause-level mutation of the replay guard. Compound predicates are mutated clause by clause because a unit mutation of this very condition reported KILLED while an individual clause inside it was both unasserted and wrong (see C3).
mutations.expected_survivor_reason: Genuine redundancy, not a coverage gap. A NULL report_run_id makes the LEFT JOIN yield a NULL run status too, so the runStatus clause alone covers every reachable state and there is nothing left to assert. The clause is KEPT because it guards the *linkedRunID dereference below, which would nil-panic if the join were ever narrowed to an inner join. C1 and C2 together are the reference instance of the third survivor class: a mutation that removes real redundancy, distinct from an invalid mutation and from a missing test.

mutations.rationale: Restores the coexistence bug, decision D14. Python allocates ReportRun.id with uuid4, so a Python-authored occurrence links an id the Go derivation cannot produce. Requiring equality failed every Go sweep that met one, and because last_run_at does not advance while a run is pending, the same due time recurs — closing the schedule's readiness for as long as such an occurrence existed. Run identity is derived to CREATE, never to RECOGNISE.

mutations.rationale: The other half of D14: the re-armed handoff must carry the LINKED run's id so its outbox dedupe key matches whatever the other runtime enqueued. Publishing the derived id would name a run that does not exist, turning a scheduler-visible fault into a permanent worker failure.

Inverts fairness to least-overdue-first. The two-pass split guarantees only AGGREGATE progress; PER-REPORT progress comes from most-overdue-first ordering. Reversed, a carried-over report is displaced by every newer arrival and starves indefinitely — the same starvation as the budget-refill bug, one level up, and the reason the bound must depend on population rather than arrival rate.

Restores the unconditional overwrite. The loop polls far more often than any schedule is due, so a window that never ran the producer cleared a live degraded reason on the very next poll — making a permanent fault visible for one poll interval and invisible to any realistic scrape. This is what made the whole per-report degraded fix unobservable in practice, so the fix and its signal must be mutated separately. Must be proved through the loop's exported metric, not the engine's returned ScheduleResult: a test that only inspects Step's return never reaches Loop.record.

Removes the tie-break, leaving the order stable rather than total. Ties are the common case, not an edge case — reports sharing a cron and last run all have the same due instant. Without the tie-break the order depends on arrival sequence, and two schedulers do NOT read the same rows because SKIP LOCKED gives each a different subset, so replica agreement would rest on a clause in another function.

Claims every window evaluated the schedule, including duplicate claims and cold-start baselines that never ran the producer. That reintroduces the M6 defect from the engine side rather than the loop side: a window with no verdict would assert one, clearing a live degraded reason. The replacement deliberately keeps `evaluated` referenced: an earlier version used `if true`, which made the variable unused and killed the mutation with a COMPILE error, so no test ran and the kill was not evidence about any assertion. Only reachable where an occurrence IS due but the producer does not run - a cold-start baseline or a duplicate claim - so a test exercising ordinary due/not-due windows cannot detect it.

Lets ErrScheduledReportUndeliverable propagate out of Produce, which is the H1 regression itself: the engine rolls the transaction back, so ONE tenant's stranded run discards every other tenant's freshly materialized run and handoff — on every tick, permanently, because last_run_at never advances while a run is pending. This pins the ISOLATION half; M26 pins detection. Python is strictly more available here, dispatching each row independently and bypassing the outbox entirely.

Drops the degraded reason from the MATERIALIZED branch, so a condition reported alongside produced work never reaches telemetry. This survived before the seam test existed: one test injected synthetic results into Loop.record without ever calling Step, another drove the real engine but asserted only returned values, so both halves were covered and the join between them was not.

Restores the promotion of an ordinary SkipReason into Degraded — a defect this change introduced into SHARED engine behaviour and that reached a producer it did not write. Because Degraded now persists until a schedule next evaluates, promoting a skip makes it latch for a full period: on the weekly remaining-metrics fan-out, 'no_active_organizations' stays raised for a week after organizations are added. A skip is 'nothing to do'; degraded is 'something is wrong'. The ledger is unaffected either way — Complete still receives the original SkipReason. Must be proved THROUGH the engine: the promotion lives in runOccurrence, so a test handing Loop.record a synthetic result never crosses the boundary the defect is on.

The pre-DDL audit must fail with exact schedule and report identities. Disabling only its positive-result clause would fall through to a raw UniqueViolation, which is the mid-migration failure CHAOS-3150 requires operators to avoid.

mutations.find: LOCK TABLE public.saved_reports IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE
mutations.replace: LOCK TABLE public.saved_reports IN SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE MODE
mutations.rationale: The audit and ALTER must observe one stable write set. SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE does not conflict with an INSERT's ROW EXCLUSIVE lock, so a duplicate can arrive after the audit and turn the planned operator error into a raw DDL failure.

Only non-null schedule ownership is unique. Multiple manual reports intentionally have NULL schedule_id; treating NULL as a duplicate would block valid installations before PostgreSQL's unique constraint, which itself permits multiple NULLs.

The storage rule is one saved report per non-null schedule_id. A named unique constraint on the already-unique primary key would let the exact ambiguous join state survive while making schema inspection look superficially complete.
The SQLAlchemy metadata used by tests and schema tooling must declare the same schedule_id invariant as Alembic. Reusing the migration's constraint name on id would create a false parity signal.

Only schedules whose durable marker is due may consume the bounded SQL page. Inverting this clause lets one tenant's 20,001 future rows fill the page and hide another tenant's due report, recreating the exact cross-tenant availability failure without the old allocation error.

The transaction may lock exactly the 500-item work budget plus one row proving a remainder. Growing that page changes the operator-facing lock-footprint contract; the proof uses an independent literal 501 rather than copying this production constant as its oracle.

mutations.find: ORDER BY replay.occurrence_id IS NOT NULL,
mutations.rationale: Never-materialized work must sort ahead of durable replays. Reversing this boolean lets the same replay population refill every bounded page under continuous arrival, so a specific carried-over report can remain due forever.

mutations.find:
FROM public.scheduled_report_occurrences AS occurrence
    WHERE occurrence.report_id = report.id
mutations.replace:
FROM public.scheduled_report_occurrences AS occurrence
    JOIN public.report_runs AS run
      ON run.id = occurrence.report_run_id
     AND run.status IN ('pending', 'running')
    WHERE occurrence.report_id = report.id
mutations.rationale: The bounded selector must not pre-decide replay semantics from run status. Terminal and link-corrupt occurrences still belong to replayExisting, which respectively stays quiet or fails visibly; filtering them here hides both states and falsely reports no due work.

A terminal transition may advance last_run_at to the exact scheduled occurrence. Equality means that occurrence is finished and the next cron instant is owed; treating it as replay suppresses the following run behind an old terminal occurrence.

A newly created report schedule must enter the SQL fairness order with the exact croniter-derived marker. Leaving it NULL makes rolling-upgrade repair consume the head of a bounded page and turns marker population into an unbounded backlog.

Changing an existing schedule's cron or report base must replace its paging marker without allocating a second job. A stale/NULL marker can misorder the report indefinitely relative to continuously arriving work.

The backfill must derive a previously-run report's next marker from last_run_at, not creation. Using creation silently reintroduces an already-consumed occurrence and moves old reports ahead of genuinely overdue work.
The migration's memory bound is a keyset loop, not a truncated first page. Stopping after one batch leaves every later report with its stale marker while still advancing the Alembic revision.
